transcript: You know that thing where someone will look at a simple contemporary painting that's just like a blue square on a red background, and they'll say, “I could have painted that.” And of course the response is always, “but you didn't.” Well, that's how I feel about shows like this. Kramer/Fauci is a verbatim theatre piece created by Daniel Fish, most known for sexy Oklahoma. And they basically perform the word for word transcript of a TV Broadcast from 1993 featuring a spirited debate between Anthony Fauci and Larry Kramer on the government's response to HlV. And i've seen several shows like this, and the response I always get is, “well, I could have just watched the TV Broadcast on youtube.” And of course the response is (say it with me) “But you didn't.” The content of the broadcast is very emotionally and intellectually stimulating and theatricalizing it puts a spotlight on it and gives it a greater sense of immediacy. And even aside from the obvious social and political weight of what they're talking about, there's also this dramatic core to the story as it paints this portrait of the love/hate relationship between these two significant figures, with frustration and deep respect going hand in hand. And even though it is performed on a mostly empty stage, there's still no shortage of theatricality in the way Daniel Fish stages it, playing with physical space in compelling ways and including some novel flourishes in the staging. Like, at one point, huge piles of soap bubbles cover the stage. Was it a little gimmicky? Maybe. But I can't deny that these stage pictures were almost as evocative as the text itself. So if this sounds up your alley: unfortunately, this very short run does close this coming saturday, february 21st And if you can't catch it, well, then I guess you can watch the original broadcast online.
